title: Painting a Grid With Three Different Colors
statement: A grid has `m` rows and `n` columns, and every one of its cells has to be given one of three colors (red, green or blue). Cells that share a side must end up with different colors. Count how many different colorings of the whole grid obey this rule, where two colorings differ if at least one cell gets a different color. The count can be huge, so return it modulo `10^9 + 7`.
notes:
## Intuition

Trying all `3^(m·n)` colorings is hopeless, but `m` is at most 5, so a single column has very few legal colorings (at most 48). A column only interacts with the column right before it, so the whole grid is a walk of `n` steps through those column patterns, where a step is allowed when the two columns differ in every row. Counting walks is a small dynamic program.

## Approach

1. Read every number `mask` below `3^m` as `m` base-3 digits, one color per row, and keep it in `columns` if no two vertically neighboring digits are equal.
2. For every pair of kept columns `i`, `j`, record `j` in `fits[i]` when no row has the same color in both, so `j` may stand to the right of `i`.
3. Let `dp[k]` be the number of ways to paint the columns so far with column pattern `k` last. For the first column every pattern gives exactly 1 way.
4. For each further column, push `dp[prev]` into `next[cur]` for every `cur` in `fits[prev]`, taking the modulus as you add.
5. The answer is the sum of `dp` modulo `10^9 + 7`.

## Example 1, step by step

With `m = 1` the masks are `0`, `1` and `2`, giving the one-cell columns `[0]`, `[1]` and `[2]`; all are legal, so `count = 3`. Each fits the two others. `dp` starts as `[1, 1, 1]`, and since `n = 1` no more columns are added, so the answer is `1 + 1 + 1 = 3`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(3^m · m + P · m + n · P), where P ≤ 48² is the number of column pairs; with `m` fixed at 5 at most this is linear in `n`.
- Space: O(P) for `fits` plus O(48) for `dp`.

## Pitfalls

- Columns must be checked twice: inside a column (vertical neighbours) when building `columns`, and between columns (horizontal neighbours) when building `fits`.
- Reduce modulo `10^9 + 7` on every addition; the sums otherwise grow past safe integers within a few dozen columns.
- When `n = 1` the loop never runs, and the answer is just the number of legal columns.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `columns` | every legal coloring of one column, as an array of colors 0–2 |
| `mask`, `rest` | the base-3 number being decoded and what is left of it |
| `fits[i]` | patterns that may stand right after pattern `i` |
| `dp[k]` | ways to paint the columns so far ending with pattern `k` |
| `next` | the same counts after adding one more column |
| `col` | index of the column being added |
